identity.title: Quantifying Frontier LLM Capabilities for Container Sandbox Escape

problem.claim: Measure whether tool-using LLM agents can escape container-based sandboxes.

contributions.claim: Introduces SandboxEscapeBench, an open benchmark for safely measuring LLM sandbox-escape capacity.
Provides an Inspect AI CTF evaluation using nested sandboxes, with the flag in an outer layer described as having no known vulnerabilities.
Covers escape mechanisms involving misconfiguration, privilege allocation, kernel flaws, and runtime/orchestration weaknesses under a motivated adversary with shell access.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their contribution as introducing the open SandboxEscapeBench benchmark.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, when vulnerabilities are added, LLMs can identify and exploit them.
The authors report that this result motivates evaluating sandboxing with SandboxEscapeBench to assess whether encapsulation continues to be provided for highly capable models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Tool-using autonomous LLM agents create security risks, while sandboxes are commonly used for isolation.
The paper introduces SandboxEscapeBench as an open measurement benchmark.
The benchmark uses an Inspect AI nested-sandbox CTF design with the flag in an outer layer described as having no known vulnerabilities.
It models a motivated shell-access adversary, spans several escape-mechanism classes, and reports exploitation of added vulnerabilities by LLMs.

source_observation.claim: The benchmark combines a threat model, multiple escape-mechanism categories, and a nested CTF architecture.

lessons.interpretation: This links the evaluation setup to the security question and makes the intended attack surface explicit.
lessons.application: For a security benchmark, state the adversary capabilities, enumerate covered failure modes, and encode the test in an isolated challenge structure.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the target system lacks a meaningful sandbox boundary or when challenge isolation cannot be established.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative results, model list, vulnerability instances, success rates, or baseline comparisons.
It does not specify how the added vulnerabilities differ from the outer layer's stated absence of known vulnerabilities or how safely the benchmark is operated.
